title: Controller instance
description: D19 (execution plan §2.6.2; queue item SPEC-REG-INSTANCE; contract in the hub-sync design §3.6). One connected copy of a controller — a phone that doses, a development build, a simulator, a lab rig, later an agent — as the body of `PUT /api/v4/instances/{instanceId}` (before 2026-10-26, `PUT <submit.href>/<vendor>/<product>/instances/<instanceId>`). It names the content-addressed definition it runs, the channel roles it plays, each with a provenance, and its labels. The instance id is the path segment: controller-supplied, opaque, a random UUID version 4 (122 random bits), never derived from a device name, model or serial. An instance carries no hardware identifiers: the upstream RFC's `ControllerInstanceRegistration` (cgm-remote-monitor docs/proposals, read at official b5ddd662) carries `device.deviceId`, `device.model`, `pumpBinding.pumpSerial` and `cgmBinding.cgmId`; this document has no such members, because the instance's purpose is to distinguish copies of a controller, which an opaque id does without identifying a person or a device. Anything identifying a controller reports is a typed, sensitivity-labelled field of its definition (D18 addendum rule 2), and the free-text `devicestatus.device` a hub observes is recorded only as a withheld observed alias (control-plane reconciliation §3.3). Must-ignore applies, as in the grammar: no object is closed. *(Amended, maintainer 2026-10-26: the instance resource is `/api/v4/instances/{instanceId}`, flat under the hub's v4 root; creating, renewing and releasing an instance use that path, and the body names the product in `product`. registration §7.)*

product.description: The product this instance is a copy of: the registration's `metadata.vendor` and `metadata.product`. Proposed with the flat instance path (maintainer, 2026-10-26): a hub serving `/api/v4/instances/{instanceId}` requires it on every PUT, refuses a request whose product is not registered (404) and a renewal naming another product than the stored instance's (422 `invalid-instance`). A hub that takes instances under the product resource reads the product from the path.

definitionId.description: The definition this instance runs: one the hub stores for this (vendor, product), named by `product` or by the path, from a product PUT or a definition PUT. Otherwise the whole instance is rejected `unknown-definition`.

roles.description: The channel roles this instance claims. The response grants or refuses each; other roles are still granted when one is refused. Each (channel, role) is claimed once.

definitionId.description: D19 rule 1: `sha256:` and the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of the definition document as submitted (a controller-owned registration, controller-state-model.schema.json).

instanceId.description: Rule 4: a random UUID version 4 in lowercase, generated by the controller for this copy, 122 random bits. Never derived from a device name, model, serial or the free-text devicestatus.device. A hub refuses any other form `invalid-instance-id`.

channel.description: Rule 5. A channel is what a role is played on. For a stateSpans kind that declares a `slot` (with no `/`), the channel is that slot name; for every other element it is `<vendor>/<product>/<element id>` (element ids as in the submit contract, e.g. `Example/Controller/extensions/com.example.feature`). A channel the instance's definition does not derive is refused `unknown-channel`. A slot channel is shared across products on the tenant only when the hub's shared slot list holds it, by name or through a declared `sameAs`; any other slot channel is the product's own, so equal unlisted names from different products do not contend (maintainer, 2026-10-16, walk-through row 5; it read 'shared across products on the tenant, so two controllers that name the same slot contend for its roles'). A `command-sink` role goes only to an instance created by the product's bound subject, or one the owner transfers it to; otherwise it is refused `not-registration-owner` (row 7).

otherTerm.description: Rule 3: the shared value `other` with the controller's own term.

roleName.description: Rule 5, open vocabulary (rule 3). `source`: the instance writes this channel's typed records as their source of record. `command-sink`: the instance accepts hub-originated commands for this channel (the kind declares `acceptsFromHub.channels` with `command`); otherwise refused `not-a-command-channel`. `other` with a term leaves room for roles such as an agent's propose and act; a hub that does not list a role in its capability document refuses it `unsupported-role`. A bare unknown string is invalid.

provenance.description: Rule 5, closed for safety. `device`: the role's data comes from, or its commands go to, real therapy hardware; only `device`-provenance data is therapy data in default views and exports. `simulated`: a simulator, a development build's simulated pump or CGM, a lab rig. One instance may mix them (a development build with a real CGM and a simulated pump).
Required. Closed: `device` or `simulated` (#/$defs/provenance). Any other value refuses this role `unknown-provenance`, never the whole instance and never accepted.

labelKey.description: Rule 7: `<namespace>/<name>`, the namespace in the reverse-DNS form extension namespaces use (`com.example.testcontroller/rig`). Labels are not subject to namespace claims. The prefix `dev.nightscout/` is reserved for the well-known keys (corrected 2026-10-15 from `nightscout.dev/`, which was not in reverse-DNS form); another key under it is refused `invalid-label`.

labels.description: Rule 7: string keys to string values, which distinguish, select and filter instances. Provenance, never a label, decides what is therapy data. Labels carry no names, device names or serials. Limits are the capability document's `instances.labels`.

dev.nightscout/purpose.description: `therapy`, `development`, `lab` or `research`; a reader reads any other value as `other`.

dev.nightscout/build.description: `release` or `dev`; a reader reads any other value as `other`.

dev.nightscout/migration-group.description: An opaque string shared by the instances of one phone migration, old and new.
